title: Repossession and Collateral Recovery Notice of Sale and Disposition Standards
content:
Standards for notices after recovery and for the disposition of the vehicle under Repossession and Collateral Recovery. Every collateral class, from Recovery Class 1 Passenger Car to Recovery Class 6 Full-Size Van, carries the same values.

| Standard | All classes |
|---|---|
| Business days after the recovery date within which the notice of intent to sell is mailed (Monday-Friday excluding federal holidays) | 3 |
| How the notice of intent to sell is delivered | certified mail, return receipt requested |
| Minimum calendar days from the notice of intent to sell mailing date to the earliest sale date stated in it (the class minimum notice period) | 15 |
| A notice returned undeliverable is re-mailed to any newer address on file, restarting the sale period | yes |
| Disposition method the company uses | private sale through a dealer auction |
| Order in which gross sale proceeds are applied | first the recovery expenses, then the contract payoff, then any surplus to the borrower |
| Calendar days after the sale within which a surplus is paid to the borrower | 10 |
| Calendar days after the sale within which the written explanation of the surplus or deficiency calculation is mailed (UCC 9-616) | 10 |
| Calendar days within which the company answers a borrower's written request for an explanation (UCC 9-616) | 14 |
| A condition report with photos is completed at intake to the storage lot | yes |

## Basis Q&A

- *Do the notice periods differ by vehicle type?* No. The class minimum notice period is 15 calendar days in all six classes, and the mailing window is 3 business days in all six.
- *What is a business day for the mailing window?* Monday to Friday, excluding federal holidays.
- *In what order is money from a sale used?* Recovery expenses first, the contract payoff second, and only what remains goes to the borrower as surplus.
